items.title: From the Financial Times: "Foreign investors are now buying more US stocks than government bonds.... International flows into US stocks reached 2.8 per cent of US GDP on average in the year to June, overtaking Treasuries — at 2 per cent of GDP — for the first time this century outside brief episodes in the Covid-19 pandemic and the aftermath of the global financial crisis, according to analysis of US Treasury data by Deutsche Bank." #economy #stocks #bonds #markets @FT

items.title: On the markets' Federal Reserve expectations: As the Fed begins its two-day FOMC meeting, culminating tomorrow in an interest rate decision and the release of updated quarterly projections, markets expect that a rate hike (currently priced at a 92% probability) will not be a "one-and-done." Rather, market pricing suggests that it will be part of a tightening cycle, with another hike expected before year-end and at least one more in the first half of 2027. (Bloomberg table below.) #economy #federalreserve #markets

items.title: Good morning. To illustrate how uncertain the current juncture is for the global economy and markets, here are four major questions. Each injects volatility into a key global price; together, they fuel systemic uncertainty: Oil: How supply disruptions evolve, alongside China's role as a "swing consumer." Yields: Whether the US Treasury will be tempted into additional market intervention to influence bond yields. The Fed: If it validates this week the market's 90% pricing of a rate hike, does this prove to be a "one and done" or the start of a tightening cycle. AI: How the balance between promise and peril is struck. #economy #markets #yields #federalreserve #oil #ai #energy
items.content:

items.title: Good morning. Further to yesterday’s post on stocks (below): Futures currently indicate that the tech-heavy Nasdaq is set to open down nearly 2%. Note that this is another area where divergence is likely IF, and it is a big IF, there is a coordinated deceleration in AI development. Specifically, a possible slowdown in the upper revenue layers need not trigger an equivalent slowdown in broader tech-related economic activity as (i) frontier models are not required for many commercial applications and, (ii) on the tech input side, numerous activities remain supply- (rather than demand-) constrained. #economy #markets #stocks #ai

items.title: Good morning. This week’s Federal Reserve policy meeting may well be the trickiest in years. Ironically, it’s less about what’s happening in the economy and more about a sudden shift in rate-hike expectations, driven by thre surge in yields ... that has less to do with the Fed and more to do with the growing ex-ante imbalance between demand for bond financing and its supply. #economy #markets #federalreserve
